market_name: Will OpenAI’s market cap be between $1.25T and $1.5T at market close on IPO day?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether any OpenAI IPO/funding-round headline coincided with the probability move; if none, treat as noise.
time_plan.1h: Compare MSFT intraday move vs QQQ/mega-cap tech beta to see if any idiosyncratic AI premium is showing.
time_plan.2h: Look for corroboration in private-market secondary indications (e.g., reported OpenAI tender valuations) or Nvidia/AI-supply-chain moves.
time_plan.6h: Re-assess whether the bracket probability shift persisted or mean-reverted; a reverting move confirms noise.
time_plan.12h: Close out research view: log whether MSFT diverged from tech index at all; expect no meaningful, attributable move.

predictions.reasoning: Microsoft holds a large economic interest in OpenAI, so OpenAI's eventual public valuation is the most direct liquid read-through. But this specific market prices a narrow $1.25T-$1.5T bracket at IPO — a conditional, distant (through end-2026), and non-binary-direction event. A shift in the implied probability of one bracket says almost nothing about whether OpenAI's value is going up or down (probability could rise because the market re-centers on a lower or higher bracket). MSFT's cap (~$3T+) also dwarfs its OpenAI stake, so even a real valuation signal is heavily diluted. Mapping is weak; direction genuinely unclear.

evidence_used: Market question prices a narrow OpenAI IPO valuation bracket ($1.25T-$1.5T) with resolution possible only upon an IPO through Dec 31, 2026
OpenAI is currently private; Microsoft is its largest outside investor and the most liquid public proxy
No IPO has been announced, making the event conditional and distant
uncertainty_notes: A probability shift on a specific bracket does not indicate valuation direction — it could reflect re-centering toward a lower or higher bracket
Microsoft's own market cap is far larger than its OpenAI stake, diluting any read-through
Nvidia and AI-chip names, or AI-themed ETFs, are alternative but even weaker proxies
The event may never resolve 'Yes' (no IPO), so time-decay dominates near-term probability moves

llm_justification.summary: This prediction market asks whether OpenAI's first-day IPO market cap lands in a narrow $1.25T-$1.5T band before end-2026. OpenAI is private, so the only liquid public proxy is Microsoft (its largest investor), with AI-ETFs/Nvidia as weaker alternatives. A move in this bracket's implied probability is a poor signal: it is conditional on an unannounced IPO, distant in time, and non-directional (probability can rise for a lower- or higher-valuation reason). Any implied valuation signal is heavily diluted in MSFT's multi-trillion cap. We flag the mapping as weak, direction unclear, and well below the 700bp tradable threshold.
key_assumptions: Microsoft is the best liquid proxy for OpenAI valuation news
Public markets have not already priced any OpenAI IPO information reflected in this market
A bracket-probability move is not accompanied by a public headline that already moved MSFT
failure_modes: The proxy is weakly exposed: MSFT cap dwarfs its OpenAI stake, so even genuine news barely moves it
Non-directional signal: a bracket probability can rise for opposite valuation reasons, so direction cannot be inferred
Already-public: any real IPO/valuation news would hit MSFT and the prediction market simultaneously, leaving no leak edge
Event may never occur (no IPO), so probability moves reflect timing/decay, not fundamentals
Move reverses as thin prediction-market liquidity mean-reverts
